title: Documentary
when: True stories, reportage, research with a human side, case studies: observed rather than presented

voice.style: warm, close and plainspoken, like someone who was there

rules: Cold open: start mid-scene on a detail (a close-up, one sound, one word), pull out to the context, and bring the title in late.
Draw the places the story happened, at the hour it happened: the clock on the wall, the harbor before dawn, the desk. Never a generic skyline.
Headings only as lower thirds (heading: bottom); names and places as captions in the picture, inside the frame.

Handheld on observed moments; lock the camera (camera: none, lens.handheld 0 on the beat) for data, so numbers read as fact. A number keeps its unit and what it is counted against, with its source in frame.
People are anonymous silhouettes lit by their world (a profile against screens), never likenesses. Quotes stay labelled until they are real and sourced.
Titles in the display serif (serif-display); bookend the film on the place or object it opened on, at a different hour.
